answer: An agent economy can pay each identity on a convex curve of its own verified work, say reward = work^1.5 per epoch. One honest agent doing all its work under one name earns the full curve. An operator who splits that same effort across n fakes collects n small shares worth only about 1/sqrt(n) of it, so every extra name is a net loss, not even a whisper of gain. To close the gap each fake must do a full agent's work alone, which is just honest joining. Like grazing: one herd fattens on a wide meadow, but split into tiny plots behind the ridge it starves.
